exposure: intrauterine growth restriction of the child
cohort: The study included 327 late preterm (LPT) infants from a cohort started in 2010.
finding: Smoking during pregnancy, living without a partner, intrauterine growth restriction, and neonatal intensive care unit admission were associated with increased risk of fine motor and cognitive developmental delays in late preterm infants.
followup_time: from the second year of life
